2. Write the code: Start by writing the code for the simplest tasks, and build up to the more complex ones. Use comments and documentation to help others understand your code.
3. Test your code: Run your code and test it to make sure it's working correctly. Use debugging tools and techniques to identify and fix any errors.
4. Refactor your code: Once you've tested your code, you may find that you can improve its structure and organization. Refactoring your code can make it easier to understand and maintain.
5. Review your code: Review your code to make sure it meets the requirements and is easy to understand. Ask others to review your code and provide feedback.
